title: El consejo a otras bibliotecas
label: ch:es-consejo
canDo: I can follow advice given to somebody else: hear what a person recommends doing, answer a question that asks the same thing with a different verb, and say that something has to be in good condition.

payoff.summary: Read the librarian's advice to anyone copying the scheme, then answer a question that swaps the verb.
payoff.note: LIKE 472, THIS CHAPTER CLEARS NO ITEM, AND FOR THE SAME REASON. Its row (mock 2 item 25) is `recomendar, empezar, estado, explicar, norma`, and after this chapter the item is blocked by EXPLICAR alone -- taught at ES-C41-explicar but deriving to B1 through SPINE-GIVE-REASONS, per HL-C418. Teaching explicar again is the duplication HL-C418 forbids. Expect 3 words taught, 2 lexemes removed, 0 items cleared. THE HL-C421 CHECK FOUND THE STEM VERB AGAIN. The row covers the passage; the stem reads `Que ACONSEJA Pardo a otras bibliotecas?` and `aconsejar` had zero hits corpus-wide, exactly as `surgir` did for item 21 in chapter 472. Two consecutive items whose question verb is absent from the book. That is now the single most productive check in the pre-check. The same sweep confirmed compañero, todavía, simpático, ayudar, traer and poco are all taught, so nothing else in those stems or options is missing. THE CHAPTER'S OWN POINT IS THE VERB SWAP. The passage says `le recomienda empezar...` and the question asks `que aconseja...?`. An exam does that deliberately: it tests the MEANING rather than the word. So the synthesis teaches the swap itself, and the two verbs are taught as one idea with two surfaces, with the lean named -- aconsejar leans toward what would be wise for you, recomendar toward what is good of its kind. THREE RULES ALREADY OWNED, ALL CITED. (1) ES-C443-acercarse OWNS THE a- PLUS WORD PLUS -ar FORMATION in as many words -- "the pattern is a- plus a word plus -ar, meaning to make it that" -- with acercar, alejar and aclarar. The aconsejar draft was re-teaching it with its own table. It now cites acercarse and adds what is genuinely new: acercarse's examples are all built on PREPOSITIONS OR ADJECTIVES, while aconsejar and acompañar (ES-C446-acompanar) are built on NOUNS, and with a noun the sense shifts from `make it that` to `supply that`. (2) ES-C34-pensar owns e-to-ie, so recomendar cites it and notes that only the SECOND e breaks. (3) ES-C431-pedido owns the participle-noun. AN OVERCLAIM CAUGHT BY THE FACT-CHECK, IN MY OWN DRAFT. estado was filed beside el pedido and la llamada as a participle hardened into a noun. That is wrong: el estado was borrowed from Latin STATUS as a noun already, and only LOOKS like estar's participle because both descend from stare. The lesson now says so explicitly -- "the shape coincides; the route does not" -- and tells the learner to file it with the family for memory while not believing they derived it. The repaso carried the same error and was corrected with it. A METHOD FLAW FOUND AND FILED IN lessons.d. This container starts with LC_ALL and LANG UNSET, so grep runs in the C locale and `.` matches ONE BYTE. In UTF-8 the ñ in acompañar is two bytes, so `grep -rln "^headword:.*acompa.ar"` returned ZERO for a word the corpus teaches with a full lesson. A false zero in the pre-check is expensive -- it is exactly how a duplicate lesson gets written. Worse, the failure is inconsistent: `compa.ero` returned four files because lesson IDS use ASCII spellings, so the pattern matched `companero` in an id while missing `compañero` in prose. The rule recorded: type the accented character, and confirm any zero a second way (lesson file, headword: line, or introduces: atom). Verified afterwards that NO word previously declared absent in chapters 468-472 is accented, so no earlier conclusion rests on the flaw. COUSIN LINKS: aconsejar takes consilium-latin from ES-C321-consejo; estado takes stare-latin from ES-C04-estar. Only mandare-latin is newly minted, for recomendar -- and it ties back to el mango in chapter 470, since mandare's hand is the same manus. `en buen estado` had already appeared in prose in ES-C461-sintesis-donar (`juguetes en buen estado`), so the phrase is handed over rather than introduced.
